APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF AUGUST 1, 2023

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Martin Herrera, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Marisol Cortez, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Richard Rojo, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Dr. Julia Ruedas, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Councilmember Puente  7-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete all
  Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council completes
  all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short recess
  and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event the City
  Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by 7:00
  p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the meeting,
  immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public wish to
  address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City Council shall
  allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to going into Closed
  Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized Closed
  Session matter shall (i) call-in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed on page
  1 of this agenda, above, prior to the City Council going into closed session; and (ii) be
  subject to a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total per
  speaker to address the City Council on any or all closed session items of business.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 4.1 through Item 4.3.

  Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
  6:02 p.m. At approximately 7:01 p.m. City Clerk Ramirez announced that the City
  Council would be in Closed Session for an additional 15 minutes. Mayor Ancona
  and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at approximately 7:26 p.m.

  Assistant City Attorney Lloyd Pilchen reported out of Closed Session with respect
  to Items 4.1 through 4.3.

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9 Subparts (a),
  (d)(2), and (e)(3) – Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation – One
  (1) Matter.

  No final reportable action taken.
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 1, 2023

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9 Subparts (a),
  (d)(2), and (e)(3) – Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation – One
  (1) Matter.

  No final reportable action taken.

  4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiators.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721); El Monte Police
  Officers Association; and El Monte Police Mid-Manager’s Association.

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Alma Martinez, City Manager and Rigoberto
  Gutierrez, Human Resources/Risk Management Director.

  No final reportable action taken.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

5.  INVOCATION:  Chaplain. Mayor Ancona

  7.1  Presentation by the City Council to Abbie Fernandez from Gidley Elementary

8.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other matter of interest to the speaker/caller that is within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing
  Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker/caller will
  be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council
  on any or all matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the
  Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on
  items of business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a
  separate allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under
  General Public Comment shall call in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed
  on page 1 of this agenda, above, by or before the General Public Comment portion of the
  agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments
  from speakers/callers who submit cards or call in to speak on matters covered by the
  section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.

  Eduardo Salazar – Spoke about the incident that happened at his property on September
  17, 2022.

  Kenneth MacKenzie – Spoke about the incident that happened at his property on
  September 17, 2022.

  Julio Ramirez – Spoke about violations at City Council meetings.

  Locke Truong – Spoke about accessory dwelling units in the City of El Monte and the
  square footage that is currently allowed.

  Armando Herman – Spoke about cannabis and drugs. Also spoke about the City Manager

  Mary Ann Powers – Spoke about an investigation regarding the cannabis license process.
  What were the results and who paid those fees.

  Edward Salcedo – Spoke about the fact that the City is very dynamic. Spoke about
  cannabis.

  Cosme Jimenez – Spoke about Councilmembers.

  Rodolfo – Spoke about Councilmembers.

  Gabriel Ramirez – Spoke about the event on Sunday celebrating Sally’s Anniversary.
  Spoke about the need to beautify the City of El Monte.

10.  DEMAND RESOLUTION NO. D-691

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA,
  ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT
  OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID.

  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA, DOES RESOLVE AS
  FOLLOWS: SECTION 1. That the attached list of claims and demands totaling
  $16,302,459.96 have been examined by the City Treasurer and that warrant numbers
  1115424 through 1115944, and the payroll ending June 30, 2023, inclusive are hereby

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  18A.1 Discussion and Update on Pioneer Park.

  Mayor Ancona – Requested an update on Pioneer Park. Assemblymember Fong
  was able to secure $500,000 for soil remediation.

  City Manager Martinez – Provided an update regarding negotiations that the City
  has had with the State Department of Parks as well as the Attorney General.

  Mayor Ancona – Had a conversation with the Governor’s Office and indicated to
  them that this is a priority for the City. If staff could provide continued updates on
  this. Would like to pick-up ideas as the City starts to reinvent Pioneer Park.

  18A.2 Update on Lifesaving Awards on Arcadia Police Department Incident.

  Mayor Ancona – Asked the Chief if there were any updates on the Lifesaving
  Awards.

  8
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 1, 2023

Chief Fisher – Provided an update to the City Council regarding this item. The
awards should be received in about two weeks.

18A.3 Discussion Regarding Rocking Wednesdays and Farmers Market.

Mayor Ancona – Asked if it was feasible to move the Farmer’s Market to the Arceo
Park Area.

City Manager Martinez – That is something that has to be discussed because this
affects the businesses.
Mayor Ancona – Requested Data a monthly report on the Farmer’s Market. The
community provided overwhelming response regarding the concerts in the park.

Mayor Pro Tem – There can be more events at Arceo Park without takimg away
from what is taking place at Farmer’s Market.

Mayor Ancona – There needs to be a Downtown Specific Plan to revitalize
Downtown.

City Manager – Staff is working on an Economic Development master plan.

18A.4 Discussion on Coordinating Council Meetings with our School District
  Partners.

Mayor Ancona – This is somethng that the City needs to participate to avoid
conflicting events.

Councilmember Martinez Muela – When can staff provide an update regarding
Coordinating Council.

City Manager – City staff is working on this to bring back to the City Council.

Mayor Ancona – Requested an update regarding the Energy Efficiency Project.

Mayor Ancona – Would like to give direction to the City Manager to reopen
negotiations with ABS. That was the will of Mayor Pro Tem’s request.

Mayor Pro Tem Herrea – Provided a quick update for the new City Council
regarding the energy efficiency project that was brought to the City Council in 2021.

Mayor Ancona – Direction given to the City Attorney’s Office to move forward with
this item.

City Manager Martinez – Had to recuse herself from this item.

18A.5 Naming of Merced Linear Park.

18A.6 Discussion and Direction on PLA.

18A.7 Discussion on Parks and Recreation Summer Programming.

18A.8 Follow Up Discussion on Fireworks Stands and Direction on Issuance of
  Future Permits (Moratorium).

Mayor Ancona – There was discusión regarding facing out how many more
fireworks will be allowed in the City. Would like to see a moratorium on firework
stands.

Councilmember Rojo – Requested follow-up on the pros and cons of the fireworks.

Councilmember Martinez Muela – Would like an update from the Chief of Police
and Fire to see a review of Fireworks.

  9

  Mayor Pro Tem Herrera – The City placed an item on the ballot and the citizens

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – provided the City Attorney with historical context

  Councilmember Puente – Would not be in favor on a moritorium of fireworks.

  Dr. Ruedas – Agreed with Councilmember Rojo. Request that data be provided
